newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen off after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen off after jobs data.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening lower on Friday after a stronger-than-expected report on July U.S. payrolls, analysts said. The following are their comments:

ROY BLUMBERG, CHIEF INVESTMENT STRATEGIST JOSEPHTHAL LYON & ROSS: "The marketplace has built in the perfect-world expectation being slow-growth, low inflation, strong corporate earnings, and anything that disrupts that expecation is going to cause temporary selling."
The government reported U.S. nonfarm payrolls grew by 316,000 jobs in July compared to a revised 228,000 jobs in June. The jobless rate stood at 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent in June.
Economists polled by Reuters had expected, on average, the report to show the economy created 193,000 new jobs in July. The unemployment rate was expected at 4.9 percent.
SHERRY COOPER, CHIEF ECONOMIST, NESBITT BURNS: "We had a very strong number and unemployment declined -- the market is not going to like that."

"But average hourly earnings were flat, which means we still have growth with no inflation, and that's going to be a mitigating factor so it won't be so bad after the market gets a chance to digest it. The prices-paid component of the NAPM is really going to be a focus now, especially after those strong Chicago numbers."
The National Association of Purchasing Management report is due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.

ARNOLD KAUFMAN, EDITOR OF STANDARD & POOR'S OUTLOOK INVESTMENT ADVISORY NEWS LETTER: "The nonfarm payrolls data was a little stronger than expected and the unemployment rate was a little lower than expected. But wages were unchanged, which is partly offsetting."

"I look for stocks to slip at the open. But while we might have a sluggish open, there will be some feeling that the good employment gains will help the economy and corporate profits, so we should recover by the close."
The 30-year bond was off 8/32 to yield 6.32 percent. The S&P 500 future was down 2.20 at 955.75.
